assessments.reasoning: The exact Ada Resource Association HTTPS location identifies the unannotated Ada 2022 Reference Manual and its Entry Calls section. The freshly retrieved page matched the pinned SHA-256, and the cited paragraph anchors resolved in those retained bytes. Section 9.5.3 paragraph 1 identifies a simple entry call as the stand-alone unconditional form for a task or protected object. Paragraph 8 places issue after name and parameter evaluation and then checks the named entry. Paragraph 12 explicitly gives queue insertion on the closed branch and places insertion inside the protected action for a protected entry. The descriptive claim reports this language for the ordinary closed outcome and excludes the exceptional routes and later execution.

challenge.method: Trace the dynamic-semantics branches in the fetched Ada 2022 section, testing an open task or protected entry, a closed protected barrier, a barrier evaluation that propagates an exception, an already completed task and a task that later completes or becomes abnormal, selection or cancellation after insertion, and the protected-barrier implementation permissions. Compare each with the condition that the check reaches paragraph 12 with an ordinary closed result.
challenge.results: Paragraphs 8 through 10 immediately select open entries. Paragraphs 6/3 and 7/3 give the normal task and protected entry tests, and paragraph 12 adds an ordinary closed call to the logical entry queue. A barrier exception leads to Program_Error for current callers under paragraph 7/3. Paragraph 21 provides Tasking_Error for the called task cases, including simple calls. Selection and cancellation under paragraphs 13 and 20 concern a call already queued. Paragraphs 23/5 and 24 permit variation in when barriers are evaluated. Paragraph 27 describes potential rechecking after insertion. These cases do not contradict insertion under the frozen condition.

limitations: The assessment concerns the text of unannotated Ada 2022 section 9.5.3 and its ordinary closed branch for issued simple entry calls. Queue servicing, completion, selection order, and other call forms are outside the conclusion.
The determination follows directly from the manual. It makes no observation about a compiler, run-time library, scheduler, or use of a physical queue.
